description: THE STOP DECISION as DATA -- the ONE step of the self-improvement loop that was still a Python drain. The jabberwock already PERCEIVES its gaps (#1), PRIORITIZES them most-salient-first (gap_prioritization: the gap_priority Argmax Program), DIAGNOSES + SELECTS + VERIFIES + APPLIES each fix (the perf/understanding drivers). What it did NOT yet DECIDE is WHEN TO STOP: the cycle simply drained the whole ordered agenda. This seed makes STOPPING the agent's OWN graph decision -- competent-man SUFFICIENCY, not completion: there is no win condition; the agent STOPS when what REMAINS is not salient enough to be worth fixing, deliberately leaving low-salience gaps UNFIXED ('sufficient -- move on; yeah yeah, the rest'). ONE graph-resident Program, the twin of perf_diagnose / gap_priority: should_continue reads the REMAINING agenda's TOP salience -- MaxOver the still-unfixed agenda gaps (Filter CapabilityGap where in_agenda==1 And Not fixed==1) by their norm_salience, default -1 when the agenda is empty -- and compares it to the SufficiencyPolicy threshold (graph data, tunable) via Gt inside an IfThenElse: CONTINUE (1.0) iff max_remaining_salience > sufficiency_threshold, else STOP (0.0). The DECISION is the Program's output, evaluated in Rust; Python only reads the boolean and breaks the loop -- it never counts, never `while gaps:`, never carries a threshold literal. The stop point MOVES with the salience DATA: RAISE a left gap's salience above the threshold and the SAME Program CONTINUES and fixes it; LOWER it and the SAME Program STOPS and leaves it. The sufficiency threshold is a stated POLICY (how much residual is 'good enough to leave'), NOT a universal metric -- tunable by editing the SufficiencyPolicy node.

microtheory.name: stopping_policy
microtheory.description: when the self-improvement cycle STOPS fixing perceived gaps: it CONTINUES iff the top remaining normalized salience exceeds the sufficiency threshold, else it STOPS and leaves the sub-threshold gaps UNFIXED. The salience is measured at the boundary; the threshold is a stated POLICY (graph data, tunable); the stop verdict is the should_continue Program's output, evaluated in Rust.

attrs.name: default_sufficiency_policy
attrs.description: the residual-salience floor below which a remaining gap is 'good enough to leave': the cycle STOPS once the top remaining normalized salience drops to or below this. A POLICY (competent-man sufficiency, ~90%-and-move-on), tunable by editing this threshold -- NOT a universal 'good enough'.
attrs.rationale: normalized salience is a residual; the two real understanding gaps sit at ~1.0 and the efficiency one-time-init at ~1.4, so a 0.5 default fixes all three real gaps (no early stop on a live boot) while any gap whose measured residual falls below 0.5 is deliberately left unfixed. Raise it to demand more sufficiency (stop sooner, leave more); lower it to fix more.
